### Global Metadata

Traditional five-piece hard rock band with male lead vocals, distorted electric guitar, electric bass, Hammond rock organ, and acoustic drum kit. 124 BPM, straight 4/4 meter. Target duration: approximately two minutes.

A confident live-band performance built around a memorable electric-guitar riff, strong bass movement, solid acoustic drums, and Hammond chord accents. The songwriting uses clear four-bar phrases, direct power-chord harmony, steady rhythmic momentum, and a focused hard-rock identity.

The emotional direction begins with sharp sarcasm and playful ridicule. The energy remains confident and driving through the main sections. The bridge naturally turns from ridicule toward restrained expectation. The final six lyric lines become sincere, determined, and encouraging while preserving the same rock-band sound.

### Vocal Details

A Chinese male rock vocalist with a clear mid-range chest voice, firm tone, precise pitch, and natural Mandarin pronunciation.

The vocal melody uses short rhythmic phrases, repeated melodic motifs, small interval movement, and clear chord-tone resolutions. Each lyric line forms one complete melodic phrase. Important syllables land on strong beats.

The verses use compact, rhythmically focused melodies. The pre-chorus rises gradually. The chorus follows a clear six-line melodic design: the first line presents the central hook, the second line answers it, the third and fourth lines develop the melody, the fifth line raises the tension, and the sixth line reaches a firm resolution.

The delivery is direct, controlled, masculine, and rhythmically precise. Notes begin cleanly and end decisively. The vocal remains closely locked to the acoustic drums, electric bass, and guitar riff.

The bridge becomes slightly calmer and more sincere across its four lines. The first two lines retain the earlier dry attitude. The third and fourth lines open the vocal tone and introduce genuine expectation.

The final six lines use broader sustained notes and a determined delivery. The team names receive clear pronunciation and strong rhythmic placement.

### Arrangement

Follow this structure:

Four-bar Intro → Verse 1 → Pre-Chorus → Chorus → Verse 2 → Four-bar Guitar Solo → Bridge → Final → Two-bar Outro.

The intro begins immediately with a four-bar distorted electric-guitar riff. Electric bass reinforces the riff accents. Hammond organ plays short rock chord stabs. The acoustic drum kit establishes a firm kick-and-snare backbeat.

Verse 1 continues the main guitar riff with palm-muted power chords, prominent bass, closed hi-hat, and steady snare. Short instrumental spaces appear between vocal phrases.

The pre-chorus opens the guitar chords, raises the Hammond voicing, and uses a compact tom fill to build tension.

The chorus expands into full distorted power chords, active bass movement, crash cymbals, and sustained Hammond chords. The vocal hook sits clearly above the band while the guitar maintains the rhythmic foundation.

Verse 2 returns to the palm-muted riff with a more active bass line and additional guitar responses between phrases.

The guitar solo lasts four bars. It develops the main riff into a concise melodic lead while bass, Hammond, and drums maintain the groove.

The bridge reduces the guitar density and lets the bass, drums, and Hammond carry the transition. The first two lines remain rhythmically compact. The third line opens the guitar voicing. The fourth line introduces a rising melodic phrase that leads directly into the final section.

The final section returns to the full-band sound. The first two lines establish a determined forward drive. The third and fourth lines rise in melodic intensity. The fifth line expands into a broad phrase. The sixth line reaches the highest emotional point and resolves on a strong sustained final note.

The outro repeats the opening riff for two bars and closes with a unified full-band final chord.

## MiniMax Music 3

A music generation model by MiniMax that creates complete songs up to 5 minutes long with stable structure and high audio quality. Two inputs drive it: **Caption** (structured music description: style, mood, vocals, arrangement) and **Lyrics** (with `[intro]` `[verse]` `[chorus]` `[bridge]` `[outro]` tags controlling song structure).

### Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Caption | Music description. Write it in three sections — Global Metadata → Vocal Details → Arrangement. The more specific, the closer the result. |
| Lyrics | Song lyrics + section tags. Tags are the only executable structural instructions; the lyric text itself only conveys mood. |
| max_duration | Target song length in seconds (default 120 = 2 minutes; the model supports up to ~300 s / 5 minutes). Longer songs take more time and VRAM. |
| seed | Random seed for the generation. Keep it fixed to reproduce the same song; change it to get a different take. |
| Model files | diffusion model / text encoder / VAE.|
| Tiled decode | Decode the audio VAE in overlapping tiles to drastically cut VRAM usage — helpful for long songs on low-VRAM GPUs. Slightly slower, with a small risk of seams at tile boundaries; turn it off on high-VRAM GPUs for the best quality. |

### Prompt Writing Guide

You can find an official [Music Caption Rewriter Skill here](https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/MiniMax-Music3)

## Report Issue
